deep.reconstruction:
This page contains no mathematics. It is a letter in German Kurrent script from Heinrich Weber, signed 'H. Weber. Professor', dated Heidelberg, 31 March 1875. It is addressed to a 'Hochgeehrter Herr Professor'. The facing draft letter to Dumas names Friedrich Wöhler of Göttingen as the person who forwarded the original, so the addressee is almost certainly Wöhler.

Content, paraphrased:
- Weber confirms receipt of the manuscript of the 'Riemannsche Abhandlung' that the addressee kindly sent him.
- He thanks the addressee for the efforts by which the editors came into possession of this posthumous work, which he calls very important for mathematicians.
- He will also thank Herr Dumas, the Secrétaire perpétuel of the Paris Académie des Sciences, for his kindness.
- He will return the manuscript as soon as he has made a copy, which will be very soon because the manuscript is short.

Context from the next page: Weber's French draft to Dumas identifies the manuscript as Riemann's original memoir for the Académie's prize competition announced in 1861. This is the heat-conduction essay, the 'Commentatio mathematica, qua respondere tentatur quaestioni ab Ill.ma Academia Parisiensi propositae'. Weber printed it, with his own commentary, in Riemann's Gesammelte mathematische Werke (1876).

The page therefore documents the provenance of the text: Académie (Dumas) → Wöhler → Weber, March 1875. Weber made a copy and returned the original to Paris. This explains why the essay sits in the 'Wärmeleitung' bundle. There is no derivation to reconstruct.

results.what: Archival/provenance record: Weber received Riemann's 1861 Paris prize memoir (heat conduction) from Wöhler, via Dumas of the Académie des Sciences, for copying for the edition of Riemann's Werke (1876).
results.modern_name: Editorial history of Riemann's 'Commentatio mathematica' (Paris prize essay on heat conduction)
results.usually_credited_to: H. Weber (editor), with R. Dedekind; Gesammelte mathematische Werke, 1876

deep.surprise_reason: This is non-mathematical editorial correspondence by Weber, not Riemann. That the Paris memoir was obtained from the Académie for the 1876 Werke is well known from Weber's editorial notes. At most it adds a precise date (31 March 1875) and the chain Dumas → Wöhler → Weber.
transcription_corrections: Top-left pencil note 'Riemann 9' and folio number '85' are archival annotations, not part of the letter.
The machine transcription is essentially correct. 'durch die wir in den Besitz' fits the image, so the '[?]' can be dropped.
The addressee 'Hochgeehrter Herr Professor' is not named on the page; the following draft to Dumas implies Wöhler (Göttingen).

Context note on the next page: Weber's draft signs as 'Professeur à l'école polytechnique de Zürich'. Weber had left Zürich around 1870 and was a professor at Königsberg in 1875, so the designation in the draft (or its transcription) deserves checking against the image.
